correctness.rationale: Fixed identity boundaries leave a freely chosen middle 231-avoider because 231 has no proper direct-sum cut; when the boundaries overlap only the identity is possible. For 1<=a,b and a+b<=n, dividing the Catalan ratio products compares factors C_t/C_(t-1) with strictly smaller-index factors, proving strictness; for overlap the direct-sum injection gives C_(n-a)C_(n-b)<=C_(2n-a-b)<C_n (including n=2). Increment expansions prove the transform statement, and fixed-threshold tail differences give convergence to independent geometrics. For t>=2 the ratio of successive Catalan ratios is exactly 1+3/((t+1)(2t-3)). Thus on a,b<=ceil(10 log_4 n) the log joint-to-product ratio is 3ab/(2n^2)+O(ab(a+b+1)/n^3); expansion and the uniform marginal estimate give a summable error after multiplication by 4^(-a-b). The rest of the covariance tail sum is bounded by O(n(n+1)^(3/2)4^(-ceil(10 log_4 n))) using 0<=Delta_(a,b)<=min(p_a,p_b), so the limit is (3/2)(4/9)^2=8/27. This is a covariance limit, not a claimed total-variation upper bound in the proof. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; its finite enumeration and rational evaluations are not needed for the all-size proof. Replay: use RESULT.md lines 18–49 and the exact ratio above.
